# michi — Agent Instructions

## Commands

- Always prefix shell commands with `rtk`.
- `just test` — run all tests (Rust + Node)
- `just test-rust` — Rust tests only (cargo nextest)
- `just check` — fmt + clippy (`--all-targets`, single workspace-wide invocation, matches CI) + deny + typos + markdown fmt
- `just pre-push` — fmt-check + `lint-affected` (moon-detected affected crates only, one multi `-p` clippy invocation — not the full workspace)
- `just build-node` — compile NAPI binary for local platform
- `just bench` — run divan benchmarks
- `just snapshots` — review insta snapshot diffs
- `just coverage` — generate lcov.info

## Non-negotiables

- No `unwrap()`/`expect()` in lib code (tests OK with message)
- No `unsafe` outside napi boundary
- `BTreeMap` for output maps, `HashMap` for internal state only
- Pre-allocate strings with `String::with_capacity`
- Truncation uses char boundaries (`floor_char_boundary`)
- Every `pub` item has a doc comment
- NAPI: `version = "3"`, `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` on every export
- Benchmarks: divan (not criterion)
- Tests: `cargo nextest run` (not `cargo test`)

## Writing

- Write docs in plain, concise language. Keep them friendly and scannable; remove filler and AI-sounding prose.
- Comments should explain non-obvious choices, stay useful, and wrap at 120 columns.

## Philosophy

- Before adding a new primitive or judging whether work is "done," read `PRINCIPLES.md` — the inclusion checklist and process conventions this project runs on.

## Architecture

- `src/` — pure sync rendering library (default features: zero runtime deps)
- `crates/michi-pipeline/` — async pipeline execution (Plan 2, shipped): `execute_pipeline`/`execute_pipeline_parallel`, `CircuitBreaker`, `CancellationToken`, its own `ExecutionError` (not a `michi_core::Error` variant — see `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`). Depends on `michi-core` + `michi-resilience` + `tokio`; not re-exported through the root `michi` facade, versioned independently.
- `packages/michi-node/` — thin NAPI cdylib shim, npm package name `@orin-axi/michi`
- Feature flags: `napi`, `serde` (opt-in Serialize/Deserialize + `toon::list()`), `schemars`, `miette`. Plan 2 execution lands as separate crates when built, never as features here — `pipeline` has shipped this way (see `crates/michi-pipeline/` above); `fuzzy`/`cache`/`cli` remain unbuilt. See `docs/spec/01-overview-and-setup.md`'s Cargo.toml section for the current split.
- See `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-03-michi-design.md` for decisions
- See `docs/spec/` for full module API reference

## Module guide

| Module | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `toon` | TOON list rendering — token-optimized agent list format |
| `kv` | Key-value single-item rendering |
| `hints` | `help[]` hint blocks |
| `truncate` | Token-safe content truncation |
| `empty` | Definitive empty state responses |
| `error` | Unified `michi::Error` type with agent rendering |
| `idempotency` | Partial-success reporting (`PartialSuccess`/`FailedOp`) — despite the name, idempotency keys and already-done detection live in `resilience` (`AlreadyDone`/`already_done()`), not here |
| `resilience` | Retry config, delay calculation, retry-after parsing |
| `status` | Health/status response rendering |
| `recovery` | Recovery hint blocks |
| `response` | `AgentResponse` builder — composes all primitives |
| `mcp` | MCP `CallToolResult` assembly — always compiled, no feature gate |
| `audience` | `Audience` (assistant/user) — shared by `mcp` and `response::render_for()` |
| `pipeline` | Pipeline pure data type + render (execution now in `crates/michi-pipeline`, not this table's `src/`) |
| `telemetry` | No-op telemetry provider (`NoopProvider`) — zero-cost default, always compiled |

# michi — Agent Instructions

## Commands

- Always prefix shell commands with `rtk`.
- `just test` — run all tests (Rust + Node)
- `just test-rust` — Rust tests only (cargo nextest)
- `just check` — fmt + clippy (`--all-targets`, single workspace-wide invocation, matches CI) + deny + typos + markdown fmt
- `just pre-push` — fmt-check + `lint-affected` (moon-detected affected crates only, one multi `-p` clippy invocation — not the full workspace)
- `just build-node` — compile NAPI binary for local platform
- `just bench` — run divan benchmarks
- `just snapshots` — review insta snapshot diffs
- `just coverage` — generate lcov.info

## Non-negotiables

- No `unwrap()`/`expect()` in lib code (tests OK with message)
- No `unsafe` outside napi boundary
- `BTreeMap` for output maps, `HashMap` for internal state only
- Pre-allocate strings with `String::with_capacity`
- Truncation uses char boundaries (`floor_char_boundary`)
- Every `pub` item has a doc comment
- NAPI: `version = "3"`, `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` on every export
- Benchmarks: divan (not criterion)
- Tests: `cargo nextest run` (not `cargo test`)

## Writing

- Write docs in plain, concise language. Keep them friendly and scannable; remove filler and AI-sounding prose.
- Comments should explain non-obvious choices, stay useful, and wrap at 120 columns.

## Philosophy

- Before adding a new primitive or judging whether work is "done," read `PRINCIPLES.md` — the inclusion checklist and process conventions this project runs on.

## Architecture

- Virtual Cargo workspace: the root `Cargo.toml` has no `[package]` and no shared version; Callisto writes each crate's `version` and keeps them equal (fixed group `michi`, lockstep releases, checked by CI version-sync)
- `crates/michi-core/` — pure sync rendering library, every primitive (default features: only `thiserror` + `compact_str`). Integration tests, divan benches and examples live in `crates/michi-core/{tests,benches,examples}` (`cargo run -p michi-core --example basic_toon`)
- `crates/michi-pipeline/` — async pipeline execution (Plan 2, shipped): validated `Plan` of `ExecStep`s, `execute`/`resume` returning a `RunRecord`, keyed `BreakerRegistry`, retry budget, `CancellationToken` (wraps tokio-util), `StepObserver`, its own `ExecutionError` (not a `michi_core::Error` variant — see `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`). API: `docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md`. Depends on `michi-core` (exact `=` version pin) + `tokio` + `tokio-util`; not re-exported through `michi-core`.
- `packages/michi-node/` — thin NAPI cdylib shim (`publish = false`), npm package name `@orin-dx/michi`; the exports themselves live in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs` behind michi-core's `napi` feature and are re-exported via `pub use michi_core::napi::*;`
- Published crates: `michi-core` and `michi-pipeline` only. There is no `michi` crate (the name on crates.io belongs to an unrelated project)
- Feature flags (on `michi-core`): `napi`, `serde` (opt-in Serialize/Deserialize + `toon::list()`), `schemars`, `miette`. Plan 2 execution lands as separate crates when built, never as features here — `pipeline` has shipped this way (see `crates/michi-pipeline/` above); `fuzzy`/`cache`/`cli` remain unbuilt. See `docs/spec/01-overview-and-setup.md`'s Cargo.toml section for the current split.
- See `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-03-michi-design.md` for decisions
- See `docs/spec/` for full module API reference

## Module guide

All modules live in `crates/michi-core/src/`.

| Module | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `toon` | TOON list rendering — token-optimized agent list format |
| `kv` | Key-value single-item rendering |
| `hints` | `help[]` hint blocks |
| `truncate` | Token-safe content truncation |
| `empty` | Definitive empty state responses |
| `error` | Unified `michi_core::Error` type with agent rendering |
| `idempotency` | Partial-success reporting (`PartialSuccess`/`FailedOp`) — despite the name, idempotency keys and already-done detection live in `resilience` (`AlreadyDone`/`already_done()`), not here |
| `resilience` | Retry config, delay calculation, retry-after parsing |
| `status` | Health/status response rendering |
| `recovery` | Recovery hint blocks |
| `response` | `AgentResponse` builder — composes all primitives |
| `mcp` | MCP `CallToolResult` assembly — always compiled, no feature gate |
| `audience` | `Audience` (assistant/user) — shared by `mcp` and `response::render_for()` |
| `pipeline` | Pipeline pure data type + render (execution lives in `crates/michi-pipeline`, not `crates/michi-core`) |
| `telemetry` | No-op telemetry provider (`NoopProvider`) — zero-cost default, always compiled |
| `napi` | NAPI export surface for `@orin-dx/michi` (`napi` feature only) — the one module allowed `unsafe` |

</INSTRUCTIONS>

# Dependency graphs (`michi-graph`)

`michi-graph` validates and orders dependency graphs: steps in a pipeline, operations in a release, packages in a workspace, tasks in an agent's plan. It is MIT-licensed, has no dependencies (it is `no_std` with `alloc`), and depends on nothing else in michi, so permissive crates such as `callisto-model` can use it. `michi-pipeline` builds its `Plan` on it.

It is a small, deterministic graph model, not a general graph library. There are no node or edge payloads, no mutation after a graph is built, no path finding and no execution policy. The reasons for each choice are in [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md), "michi-graph: an MIT leaf crate, versioned on its own".

## Vocabulary

- A **node** has a key `K: Ord + Clone` chosen by the caller (`StepId`, `PackageId`, `String`).
- An **edge** says that a **dependent** depends on a **prerequisite**: the prerequisite comes first. The API never says "from/to" or "in/out", because those words mean opposite things in different tools.
- Every edge has a **kind** `E: Ord`, which defaults to `()`. Callisto uses kinds such as runtime, dev and peer; michi and wisp don't use kinds.
- A `NodeIx` is a node's declaration position: the first node declared is 0. It has no public constructor. Every method that takes one returns an empty slice or `None` for an index the graph does not have, so an index from another graph never panics.

## Building

```rust
let mut b = GraphBuilder::<StepId>::with_capacity(steps.len());
for step in &steps {
    let node = b.node(step.id().clone());
    for prerequisite in step.prerequisites() {
        b.depends_on(node, prerequisite, ());
    }
}
let graph = b.build(UnknownTargets::Error);
```

- `node(key)` declares a node and returns a `Decl` token. Edges hang off the token, not the key. A later node reusing a key is recorded as a duplicate, and its edges are dropped with it, so they can never land on the first node and cause false errors.
- `depends_on(decl, prerequisite, kind)` takes the prerequisite key, which may be declared before or after. An edge repeated with the same kind collapses into one.
- `build(policy)` never fails. It sets aside what it cannot use and records why, so every problem can be reported later in one list:
  - a duplicate node;
  - an edge to a key no node has (a **dangling** edge). It is always kept in `Graph::dangling()`. The `UnknownTargets` policy only decides whether validation reports it: `Error` reports it as `UnknownDependency`, and `Ignore` doesn't (Callisto ignores dependencies on packages outside the workspace);
  - more than `u32::MAX` nodes.
- A node that depends on itself is kept as an ordinary edge, and the edge filter decides whether it counts (a dev-only self-dependency is legal in Cargo).
- `Dag::from_nodes(iter, order)` builds and validates in one call for the common case: no kinds and unknown targets are errors.

## Graph and Dag

A `Graph<K, E>` may contain cycles. A `Dag<K>` is proven acyclic and carries no kinds, because validation has already chosen which edges count.

- `graph.validate(order)` uses every edge; `graph.validate_filtered(keep, order)` keeps only the edges for which `keep(EdgeRef)` returns true. `EdgeRef` has named fields: `dependent`, `prerequisite`, `kind` and both `NodeIx`s. Keys are shared between the graph and its dags, so validating does not copy them.
- One graph can produce several dags. Callisto validates its package graph once without dev edges for cascade order, and once with them for publish order.
- Validation returns the `Dag` or a `Violations` list with every problem at once. Cycles made only of filtered-out edges are not problems: you validate the graph you will run.
- When several kinds connect the same pair and more than one passes the filter, the dag holds one edge. `prerequisites` and `dependents` never repeat a node.
- `graph.cycles(keep, order)` reports the cycles of a graph that is allowed to have them (lumen's agent trajectories).

## Order

The caller chooses how ties are broken, once, at validation:

- `Order::Declaration`: the earliest-declared node first. Steps run in the order they were written. michi uses this.
- `Order::Key`: the smallest key first. Shuffling the declarations changes nothing. Callisto uses this, because it seals its release plan with a digest.

Everything the crate outputs follows that one order: the topological order, each layer, `ready`, `ancestors`, `descendants`, cycle members and the order of the violations' cycles. The topological order is the lexicographically smallest valid order under that rule, and that is part of the contract, not an implementation detail. The order never comes from hash maps or traversal accidents.

## Queries on a Dag

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `order()` | `&[NodeIx]` in topological order, computed at validation |
| `keys_in_order()` | the keys in that order |
| `prerequisites(ix)`, `dependents(ix)` | `&[NodeIx]` neighbours, in the chosen order |
| `layers()` | layer 0 has no prerequisites; a node's layer is one more than its deepest prerequisite's. Nodes in one layer don't depend on each other, so they can run together |
| `ready(satisfied, eligible)` | nodes for which `eligible(key)` holds and `satisfied(p)` holds for every prerequisite, in order |
| `ancestors(roots)`, `descendants(roots)` | every node upstream or downstream of `roots`, not including them |
| `key(ix)`, `index_of(&key)`, `node_at(position)`, `len()` | lookups; `node_at` maps a declaration position to its node, for callers that keep per-node data in declaration order |
| `canonical()` | each node's key with its prerequisites' keys, nodes and prerequisites sorted by key, for callers that hash the structure with their own hasher. Isolated nodes are included |

`ready` takes two predicates because callers track more than "done". A node behind a failure must not become ready, and a running or failed node is not eligible to start. When `satisfied` holds only for nodes that succeeded, checking direct prerequisites is enough: a node whose prerequisite failed can never become ready.

`ready` is one pass over the graph, O(V + E). There is no incremental ready tracker: michi's scheduler keeps its own counters because what unblocks a step depends on the outcome, and Callisto's release plans are small. A tracker can be added later without a breaking change if a consumer measures a need.

## Violations

`Violation<K>` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and holds keys, cloned only on the error path:

- `DuplicateNode { key }`
- `UnknownDependency { dependent, prerequisite }`
- `SelfDependency { key }`: reported once per node, never as a cycle.
- `Cycle(Cycle<K>)`: `members()` lists every node of one strongly connected component, in the chosen order. `path()` is one shortest closed path through the first member, so a message can show a real loop.
- `TooManyNodes`

`Violations<K>` lists them in a fixed order: duplicates, then edge problems by the dependent's declaration position and the edge's position, then cycles in the chosen order. The same input always gives the same list.

`Display` exists when `K: Display`, and `display_with(|key, f| ...)` covers keys without it. A cycle reads as `a depends on b, which depends on c, which depends on a`. The printed path stops after 8 steps with `… and N more`; the struct keeps the whole path. `Violations<K>` implements `core::error::Error` when `K: Debug + Display`.

## Implementation rules

- No recursion: Kahn's algorithm for the order and an iterative Kosaraju for strongly connected components. A 100,000-node chain and a 100,000-node cycle are tested.
- Kahn's leftovers are always an error: nodes on or behind a cycle never disappear silently. Strongly connected components are computed only on those leftovers, so a valid graph doesn't pay for them.
- Adjacency is `u32` indices in sorted vectors; keys live once in an `Arc<[K]>`, and a key-sorted index permutation answers `index_of` by binary search.
- No `unwrap`, `expect`, unchecked indexing or `unsafe` (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`).

## How michi-pipeline uses it

- `Plan::new` declares one node per step, builds with `UnknownTargets::Error` and validates with `Order::Declaration`. Violations map one to one onto `PlanViolation`. Cycles stay a single `PlanViolation::Cycle` listing every step on any cycle in declaration order, and `TooManyNodes` becomes `PlanViolation::TooManySteps`. One change: a step stuck between two cycles (depending on one, depended on by another) lies on no cycle and is no longer listed.
- The scheduler reads `order()`, `prerequisites` and `dependents`. Node indices are declaration positions, so they match `Plan::steps()` and `RunRecord` without translation. Its ready counters, failure skipping and resume seeding stay in michi-pipeline: they are execution policy.
- `PlanFingerprint` stays michi's own 64-bit FNV-1a with its current framing, computed over `canonical()`. A record saved before the change still resumes.
- No michi-graph type appears in michi-pipeline's public API, so a michi-graph release never forces a breaking michi-pipeline release. michi-pipeline depends on it with a normal `^` range, not the exact pin the lockstep crates use.

## Licensing and release

- `license = "MIT"` in the crate's own manifest and a crate `LICENSE`; the rest of the workspace stays FSL-1.1-MIT.
- CI walks the normal and build dependencies of `michi-graph` with `cargo metadata` and fails on any license outside the permissive allowlist, so no FSL crate can enter its tree.
- It versions on its own, outside the Callisto fixed group `michi`. A michi-graph minor release moves michi-pipeline out of its `^` range, so Callisto's cascade also bumps the michi group.

# Principles

Two questions come up over and over: **should this go in michi?** and **how should this work get done?** This doc answers both, so nobody — human or agent — has to re-derive the reasoning from scratch each time. It's the "why" behind `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s rules, not a replacement for either.

---

## What belongs in michi

A primitive earns a place here only if it clears all five gates below. These are yes/no checks with evidence, not vibes — if you can't point to the evidence, it doesn't clear the gate yet.

### 1. Rendering, not domain logic

It turns already-decided data into agent-readable strings/types. It doesn't decide _what_ data survives.

- One established exception: char/byte-level truncation (`truncate`, `ToonOptions::max_cell_len`) — treated as rendering safety, not business logic.
- **The ceiling:** if a tool's real need is more sophisticated than a generic primitive can serve — a custom ranking algorithm, a heuristic tuned to one tool's data shape — that's a sign the primitive doesn't belong in michi, not a sign to make michi's primitive more complex. See [Split the decision from the signal](#split-the-decision-from-the-signal) for how to resolve this without compromising on either.

### 2. Small default dependency set

The default build depends only on `thiserror` and `compact_str`. Anything else is opt-in behind a Cargo feature.

- Adding a mandatory dependency needs a recorded decision in `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`. Prefer caller-supplied injection (a closure, a trait) first.

### 3. Genuinely cross-tool — verified, not assumed

Earns inclusion when independent, real tools would otherwise hand-roll the identical pattern.

- "Independent" and "real" are load-bearing. One tool using a pattern heavily is one data point, not proof.
- **What clearing this bar looks like:** a survey across several real agent-facing dev tools (a code-search engine, a CLI proxy, a context-compression tool, a code-graph server) found `help[]`-shaped "note for the agent" hints independently reinvented, inconsistently, in every one of them.
- A pattern seen in only one tool — however heavily repeated inside that tool — isn't there yet. Watch for a second independent confirmation before building it.

# 7. Pipeline execution: plans, run records and replay safety

Status: Accepted

## Context

`michi-pipeline`'s positional executors (`execute_pipeline`, `execute_pipeline_parallel`, `StepDependencies`) mutated a shared `Pipeline`, bound runners to list positions, could not resume, and reported "not run" and "ran and failed" with the same status. A retry or replay could repeat work that had already taken effect.

## Decision

Rebuild execution around a validated plan, one scheduler and an immutable run record, following the research report's nine ranked changes.

- **Identity:** `StepId` and `RunId` are caller-chosen slugs, so agents can read and echo them and `run_id:step_id` is a stable idempotency key.
- **Plan:** an immutable `Plan` is validated once and reports every violation before anything runs. Its fingerprint binds a record to the plan for resume.
- **Record:** `execute` returns a `#[must_use]` `RunRecord` with exactly one terminal status and a reason per step. `RunOutcome` is `Succeeded` only if every plan step succeeded.
- **Replay rule:** every failed attempt is not executed, rejected, ambiguous or definitive. Ambiguous outcomes (timeout, 502, 504, cancellation in flight) of a non-idempotent step end `OutcomeUnknown` and are never replayed automatically.
- **Resume:** `resume` runs under the record's run id, never re-runs completed steps, and re-runs unknown outcomes only if the step is idempotent or the caller verified it. It is at least once per step; exactly once needs a deduplicating downstream.

- Keep the positional executors and add resume. Rejected: position-bound runners and a mutated pipeline cannot give a stable step identity or a trustworthy record.
- A workflow engine or DAG crate (dagrs, petgraph, tower `Service` steps, a retry crate). Rejected: each adds a model or a second source of backoff truth, and none has the replay classification.
- Durable storage, sagas, data passing between steps. Out of scope: michi is an embeddable step runner, not an orchestrator.

- The record format is strict. `michi-graph` validates and orders dependency graphs: steps in a pipeline, operations in a release, packages in a workspace, tasks in an agent's plan. It is MIT-licensed, has no dependencies (it is `no_std` with `alloc`), and depends on nothing else in michi, so permissive crates such as `callisto-model` can use it. `michi-pipeline` builds its `Plan` on it.

It is a small, deterministic graph model, not a general graph library. There are no node or edge payloads, no mutation after a graph is built, no path finding and no execution policy. The reasons for each choice are in [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md), "michi-graph: an MIT leaf crate, versioned on its own".

## Vocabulary

- A **node** has a key `K: Ord + Clone` chosen by the caller (`StepId`, `PackageId`, `String`).
- An **edge** says that a **dependent** depends on a **prerequisite**: the prerequisite comes first. The API never says "from/to" or "in/out", because those words mean opposite things in different tools.
- Every edge has a **kind** `E: Ord`, which defaults to `()`. Callisto uses kinds such as runtime, dev and peer; michi and wisp don't use kinds.
- A `NodeIx` is a node's declaration position: the first node declared is 0. It has no public constructor. Every method that takes one returns an empty slice or `None` for an index the graph does not have, so an index from another graph never panics.

## Building

```rust
let mut b = GraphBuilder::<StepId>::with_capacity(steps.len());
for step in &steps {
    let node = b.node(step.id().clone());
    for prerequisite in step.prerequisites() {
        b.depends_on(node, prerequisite, ());
    }
}
let graph = b.build(UnknownTargets::Error);
```

- `node(key)` declares a node and returns a `Decl` token. Edges hang off the token, not the key. A later node reusing a key is recorded as a duplicate, and its edges are dropped with it, so they can never land on the first node and cause false errors.
- `depends_on(decl, prerequisite, kind)` takes the prerequisite key, which may be declared before or after. An edge repeated with the same kind collapses into one.
- `build(policy)` never fails. It sets aside what it cannot use and records why, so every problem can be reported later in one list:
  - a duplicate node;
  - an edge to a key no node has (a **dangling** edge). It is always kept in `Graph::dangling()`. The `UnknownTargets` policy only decides whether validation reports it: `Error` reports it as `UnknownDependency`, and `Ignore` doesn't (Callisto ignores dependencies on packages outside the workspace);
  - more than `u32::MAX` nodes.
- A node that depends on itself is kept as an ordinary edge, and the edge filter decides whether it counts (a dev-only self-dependency is legal in Cargo).
- `Dag::from_nodes(iter, order)` builds and validates in one call for the common case: no kinds and unknown targets are errors.

## Graph and Dag

A `Graph<K, E>` may contain cycles. A `Dag<K>` is proven acyclic and carries no kinds, because validation has already chosen which edges count.

- `graph.validate(order)` uses every edge; `graph.validate_filtered(keep, order)` keeps only the edges for which `keep(EdgeRef)` returns true. `EdgeRef` has named fields: `dependent`, `prerequisite`, `kind` and both `NodeIx`s. Keys are shared between the graph and its dags, so validating does not copy them.
- One graph can produce several dags. Callisto validates its package graph once without dev edges for cascade order, and once with them for publish order.
- Validation returns the `Dag` or a `Violations` list with every problem at once. Cycles made only of filtered-out edges are not problems: you validate the graph you will run.
- When several kinds connect the same pair and more than one passes the filter, the dag holds one edge. `prerequisites` and `dependents` never repeat a node.
- `graph.cycles(keep, order)` reports the cycles of a graph that is allowed to have them (lumen's agent trajectories).

## Order

The caller chooses how ties are broken, once, at validation:

- `Order::Declaration`: the earliest-declared node first. Steps run in the order they were written. michi uses this.
- `Order::Key`: the smallest key first. Shuffling the declarations changes nothing. Callisto uses this, because it seals its release plan with a digest.

Everything the crate outputs follows that one order: the topological order, each layer, `ready`, `ancestors`, `descendants`, cycle members and the order of the violations' cycles. The topological order is the lexicographically smallest valid order under that rule, and that is part of the contract, not an implementation detail. The order never comes from hash maps or traversal accidents.

## Queries on a Dag

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `order()` | `&[NodeIx]` in topological order, computed at validation |
| `keys_in_order()` | the keys in that order |
| `prerequisites(ix)`, `dependents(ix)` | `&[NodeIx]` neighbours, in the chosen order |
| `layers()` | layer 0 has no prerequisites; a node's layer is one more than its deepest prerequisite's. Nodes in one layer don't depend on each other, so they can run together |
| `ready(satisfied, eligible)` | nodes for which `eligible(key)` holds and `satisfied(p)` holds for every prerequisite, in order |
| `ancestors(roots)`, `descendants(roots)` | every node upstream or downstream of `roots`, not including them |
| `key(ix)`, `index_of(&key)`, `node_at(position)`, `len()` | lookups; `node_at` maps a declaration position to its node, for callers that keep per-node data in declaration order |

`ready` is one pass over the graph, O(V + E). There is no incremental ready tracker: michi's scheduler keeps its own counters because what unblocks a step depends on the outcome, and Callisto's release plans are small. A tracker can be added later without a breaking change if a consumer measures a need.

## Violations

`Violation<K>` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and holds keys, cloned only on the error path:

- `DuplicateNode { key }`
- `UnknownDependency { dependent, prerequisite }`
- `SelfDependency { key }`: reported once per node, never as a cycle.
- `Cycle(Cycle<K>)`: `members()` lists every node of one strongly connected component, in the chosen order. `path()` is one shortest closed path through the first member, so a message can show a real loop.
- `TooManyNodes`

`Violations<K>` lists them in a fixed order: duplicates, then edge problems by the dependent's declaration position and the edge's position, then cycles in the chosen order. The same input always gives the same list.

`Display` exists when `K: Display`, and `display_with(|key, f| ...)` covers keys without it. A cycle reads as `a depends on b, which depends on c, which depends on a`. The printed path stops after 8 steps with `… and N more`; the struct keeps the whole path. `Violations<K>` implements `core::error::Error` when `K: Debug + Display`.

## Implementation rules

- No recursion: Kahn's algorithm for the order and an iterative Kosaraju for strongly connected components. A 100,000-node chain and a 100,000-node cycle are tested.
- Kahn's leftovers are always an error: nodes on or behind a cycle never disappear silently. Strongly connected components are computed only on those leftovers, so a valid graph doesn't pay for them.
- Adjacency is `u32` indices in sorted vectors; keys live once in an `Arc<[K]>`, and a key-sorted index permutation answers `index_of` by binary search.
- No `unwrap`, `expect`, unchecked indexing or `unsafe` (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`).

- `Plan::new` declares one node per step, builds with `UnknownTargets::Error` and validates with `Order::Declaration`. Violations map one to one onto `PlanViolation`. Cycles stay a single `PlanViolation::Cycle` listing every step on any cycle in declaration order, and `TooManyNodes` becomes `PlanViolation::TooManySteps`. One change: a step stuck between two cycles (depending on one, depended on by another) lies on no cycle and is no longer listed.
- The scheduler reads `order()`, `prerequisites` and `dependents`. Node indices are declaration positions, so they match `Plan::steps()` and `RunRecord` without translation. Its ready counters, failure skipping and resume seeding stay in michi-pipeline: they are execution policy.
- `PlanFingerprint` stays michi's own 64-bit FNV-1a with its current framing, computed over `canonical()`. A record saved before the change still resumes.
- No michi-graph type appears in michi-pipeline's public API, so a michi-graph release never forces a breaking michi-pipeline release. michi-pipeline depends on it with a normal `^` range, not the exact pin the lockstep crates use.

## Licensing and release

- `license = "MIT"` in the crate's own manifest and a crate `LICENSE`; the rest of the workspace stays FSL-1.1-MIT.
- CI walks the normal and build dependencies of `michi-graph` with `cargo metadata` and fails on any license outside the permissive allowlist, so no FSL crate can enter its tree.
- It versions on its own, outside the Callisto fixed group `michi`. A michi-graph minor release moves michi-pipeline out of its `^` range, so Callisto's cascade also bumps the michi group.

# Pipeline execution (`michi-pipeline`)

`michi-pipeline` runs a static graph of async steps on Tokio and returns a record of what happened to each one. It is an embeddable library, not an orchestrator: there is no server, no persistence, no scheduling across runs and no dynamic dependencies. What it adds over a plain `JoinSet` is the part agents need: an honest status for every step, retries that never blindly replay work that may already have taken effect, and a resume that continues an interrupted run without repeating finished steps.

This document describes the API that replaced `execute_pipeline`, `execute_pipeline_parallel` and `StepDependencies` (see [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md), "Pipeline execution redesign"). The design follows the research report in [`docs/research/pipeline-design.md`](../research/pipeline-design.md).

## Identity

- `StepId` names a step. It is chosen by the caller, unique within a plan, and meant to be read and copied by agents, so it is a short slug: 1 to 64 ASCII characters, letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, starting with a letter, digit or `_`. `StepId::try_new` rejects anything else with an `IdError` (`Empty`, `TooLong`, `InvalidChar`). Ids never contain `:`, so the idempotency key below is unambiguous.
- A step's `name` is free-form display text and may repeat.
- `RunId` names one run. It has the same charset. The caller supplies it, because only the caller knows what a run is (one agent request, one job). `RunId::unique(prefix)` builds `{prefix}-{millis}-{pid}-{counter}` (numbers in base 36, each after its own `-`, so two processes cannot print the same digits) without a UUID dependency.
- Reusing a `RunId` for a different plan or different inputs is the caller's mistake and michi cannot detect it: downstream services that deduplicate on the idempotency key would treat the new work as a repeat.

## Plan

A step definition is an `ExecStep`: an id, a name, the ids it depends on, the runner (`impl Step`) and optional per-step overrides (retry policy, per-attempt timeout, total step deadline, breaker key).

`Plan::new(steps)` validates the whole definition before anything runs and returns either an immutable `Plan` or a `PlanError` listing every violation at once:

- `DuplicateStepId`: a later step reuses an earlier step's id.
- `UnknownDependency`: a step depends on an id no step has.
- `SelfDependency`: a step depends on itself.
- `Cycle`: the steps that lie on a dependency cycle, found without recursion, so graph depth is bounded by memory rather than the call stack.
- `TooManySteps`: more than `u32::MAX - 1` steps.

Validation and ordering come from [`michi-graph`](09-graph.md); no michi-graph type appears in this crate's API.

A repeated dependency in one step's list is collapsed. An invalid plan is an `Err` before execution, so it can never be confused with a run that happened and failed.

`Plan::execution_order()` is the dry run: the order sequential mode dispatches steps in, which is topological order with ties broken by declaration order. `Plan::fingerprint()` is a stable 64-bit FNV-1a hash over each step's id and dependency ids, independent of declaration order. Names, runners and options are not part of it, because closures cannot be hashed.

## Steps

```rust
pub trait Step: Send + Sync {
    fn run<'a>(&'a self, ctx: &'a StepContext) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<(), ExecutionError>> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn replay(&self) -> Replay { Replay::NotIdempotent }
}
```

Steps return `()`: they act through side effects and share state through `Arc` captures. Outputs do not flow between steps.

`StepContext` carries the run id, step id, attempt number (0-based), a cancellation token that is a child of the run's token, and the step's deadline if one is set. `idempotency_key()` is `run_id:step_id`. It stays the same across attempts and across resume, so a step that passes it to a deduplicating downstream gets each effect applied once. The attempt number is for logging and backoff only and is never part of the key.

`step_fn(|ctx| async move { ... })` adapts a closure. `FnStep::idempotent()` opts it in to `Replay::Idempotent`.

## Replay rule

Every failed attempt is classified by whether it could have taken effect (RFC 9110 §9.2.2). The same class decides whether the executor retries, which terminal status the step ends in, and whether the returned error says replay is safe.

| Class | Errors | Retried | Terminal status if it is the last outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Not executed | `CircuitOpen` or `Cancelled` returned by the step | `CircuitOpen` after its `retry_after`; `Cancelled` no | `NotRun(CircuitOpen)`; for `Cancelled`, `Skipped(Cancelled)` if the run was cancelled, otherwise `Failed` |
| Rejected | HTTP 429 and 503, `Failed { retryable: true }` | yes, every step | `Failed` |
| Ambiguous | timeouts, HTTP 502 and 504, `Interrupted`, `AmbiguousOutcome` | only `Replay::Idempotent` steps | idempotent: `Failed`; otherwise `OutcomeUnknown` |
| Definitive | everything else | no | `Failed` |

Treating 429 and 503 as "not processed" is a convention, not an RFC guarantee, so a step that may have committed its effect must not report them. It reports 502, 504, a timeout or a non-retryable error instead. A step returns `Cancelled` only when it stopped without effect.

A step that returns `Cancelled` while the run's token has not fired cancelled itself (its own timer or token, say). Nothing upstream asked it to stop, so it is not a consequence of anything: it ends `Failed`, a root cause whose dependents are skipped with `caused_by` naming it. It never took effect, so resume runs it again like any failed step.

A server's `retry_after` (on `Http` or `CircuitOpen`, also inside `StepFailed`) is waited in full, even past `RetryConfig::max_delay`: the server said when to come back, and coming back sooner only earns another rejection. `max_delay` caps michi's own exponential backoff (michi-core's `next_retry_delay` keeps that cap; the pipeline applies the server rule on top). The step deadline still bounds the wait: if the wait would end at or past the deadline, the step stops retrying at once and its reason ends `step deadline reached`. Without a deadline, a long hint is waited out, and cancellation interrupts the wait.

A non-idempotent step whose last outcome is ambiguous ends `OutcomeUnknown` and its error is wrapped in `ExecutionError::AmbiguousOutcome`, which is not retryable and converts to a `DomainError` telling the agent to verify whether the operation completed. An idempotent step's ambiguous outcome stays bare and retryable.

## Status model

`michi_core::pipeline::StepStatus` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, as are its reason enums. Each terminal status maps to one recovery verb.

| Status | Meaning | Agent verb |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Pending` | not started | none yet |
| `Running` | in flight (only seen in records persisted from `on_step_started`) | resume treats it as ambiguous |
| `Completed` | ran and succeeded in this run | none |
| `CompletedEarlier` | succeeded in an earlier attempt of this run, not re-run by resume | none |
| `Failed` | ran and failed, definitively or with a replay-safe error | fix the cause, then resume |
| `OutcomeUnknown(cause)` | may have taken effect: `Timeout`, `Gateway` (502/504), `Cancelled` (dropped mid-flight after cancellation), `Interrupted` (in flight when the process stopped) | verify, then resume |
| `Skipped(PrerequisiteFailed)` | a prerequisite did not complete | fix the root cause, then resume |
| `Skipped(Cancelled)` | cancelled before it took effect | resume |
| `NotRun(CircuitOpen)` | its circuit breaker was open, so it was never invoked | wait, then resume |
| `Panicked` | the step's code panicked: a harness failure, not a step error | fix the bug, verify, then resume |

`Pipeline::render()` emits `step[N]{id,name,status,reason}:` with snake_case labels (`completed_earlier`, `outcome_unknown`, `not_run`, ...) and a reason (`prerequisite_failed`, `cancelled`, `circuit_open`, `timeout`, `gateway`, `interrupted`) or `null`. It stays TOON 4.4 conformant.

## Run record

`execute(&plan, run_id, &opts).await` returns a `#[must_use]` `RunRecord` with private fields and accessors. It never returns an error: a run that happened is a record, however it went.

- `run_id()`, `plan_fingerprint()`, `elapsed()`, `was_cancelled()` (the caller's token fired), `observer_panics()` (observer calls that panicked; see Observer).
- `steps()`: one `StepRecord` per plan step, in declaration order. Each has the step id, name, terminal status, a human-readable `reason`, the final `error`, every attempt (number, replay class of its failure, error text, elapsed time), when it started relative to the run, how long it took, and for a consequential skip the root-cause step (`caused_by`).
- `outcome()`: `Succeeded` only if the record lists every plan step and each is `Completed` or `CompletedEarlier`. Otherwise `OutcomeUnknown` if any step's outcome is unknown (`OutcomeUnknown`, or `Running` in a rebuilt record), else `Cancelled` if the caller cancelled, else `Failed`. A skipped, not-run, pending, running or panicked step therefore never reads as success.
- `root_causes()`: steps that failed in their own right (`Failed`, `OutcomeUnknown`, `NotRun`, `Panicked`, and `Running` in a rebuilt record). `consequential()`: skipped steps. An agent sees one cause instead of N errors.
- `needs_verification()`: every step resume holds until the caller verifies it (unless it is idempotent): `OutcomeUnknown`, `Panicked` and `Running`. These are exactly the steps `ResumeOptions::verified` accepts (`StepRecord::awaits_verification()`).
- `completion_order()`: ids of steps that completed in this run, in the order they finished, so callers can compensate if they choose to.
- `error()`: the first root cause as `ExecutionError::StepFailed`, which converts to `DomainError`. When no step failed in its own right (a cancelled run, or a rebuilt record with pending steps) it names the first step that did not succeed, so `error()` is `None` only for a `Succeeded` run.
- `to_pipeline()` and `render()`: the michi-core `Pipeline` view and its TOON.

A record always holds exactly one `StepRecord` per plan step, in declaration order, and stores the plan's step count, so a record that lost steps cannot read as a success.

With the `serde` feature, `RunRecord`, `StepRecord`, `ExecutionError` and the ids serialize, so callers can persist records. The serialized record carries `plan_steps`; deserializing fails if `steps` does not list that many distinct steps (a missing or repeated step), so a truncated or tampered record is an error rather than a success. Records saved by 0.3 lack `plan_steps` and must be re-saved (or have `"plan_steps": <step count>` added).

`RunRecord::from_parts(run_id, saved_fingerprint, &plan, steps)` rebuilds a record from step records saved one at a time. It returns `ResumeError::FingerprintMismatch` if the saved fingerprint is not the plan's and `ResumeError::UnknownStep` for a saved step the plan lacks. When `steps` holds several records for one step, the last one wins, so an append-only log of `StepRecord::in_flight` on start and the finished record on finish rebuilds each step's latest status. A plan step with no saved record is `Pending`.

## Scheduling

One scheduler loop drives both modes. It keeps a remaining-prerequisite count per step and a ready set ordered by declaration index, and spawns ready steps onto a `tokio::task::JoinSet` owned by the call, so no step outlives `execute` or `resume`.

- `Mode::Sequential` (default): one step at a time, in `Plan::execution_order()`.
- `Mode::Parallel { max_concurrency: NonZeroUsize }`: the loop dispatches ready steps in declaration order while fewer than `max_concurrency` are running. The cap lives in the dispatch loop, not in a semaphore inside spawned tasks, so admission order is declaration order rather than wake order.

`FailurePolicy` decides what a failure does to the rest of the run:

- `SkipDependents` (default): the failed step's transitive dependents are `Skipped(PrerequisiteFailed)` and independent branches keep running. This applies in sequential mode too, which changes the old behaviour of stopping at the first failure.
- `FailFast`: the first failure stops dispatching and cancels the run's token. Running steps get the cancellation grace period to finish, then their attempts are dropped and they end `OutcomeUnknown(Cancelled)` (or `Failed` if idempotent). Steps never started end `Skipped(Cancelled)`.

A step that panics is caught through its `JoinError` and ends `Panicked`. Other steps keep running and the breaker probe it held, if any, is released.

## Cancellation and time

`CancellationToken` wraps tokio-util's token, so tokio-util's 0.x type is not part of michi's public API. `ExecOptions::cancellation(token)` installs the caller's token; the run uses a child of it, and each step gets a child of the run token in its context.

When the token fires, nothing new is dispatched and every step not yet started ends `Skipped(Cancelled)`. A running attempt can watch `ctx.cancellation()` and stop cooperatively by returning `ExecutionError::Cancelled`, which also ends `Skipped(Cancelled)`. If it is still running after the grace period (`ExecOptions::cancel_grace`, default 5 s), its future is dropped and it ends ambiguous. Backoff sleeps race the token, so a cancelled run never waits out a retry delay.

Each attempt runs under `tokio::time::timeout` (`attempt_timeout`, default 30 s). An optional total deadline (`step_deadline`) bounds a step across all its attempts and backoff: no attempt starts or sleeps past it, and the last attempt is cut to the time left. A deadline too far away for the clock to represent (such as `Duration::MAX`) means no deadline; it never panics. All time is `tokio::time`, so tests run on a paused clock.

## Breakers and budgets

Circuit breakers are keyed. A `BreakerRegistry` holds one breaker per key, created on first use with the registry's `BreakerConfig`. A step's key is `ExecStep::breaker_key` (for example, one key per downstream service) and defaults to its step id. Pass the same `Arc<BreakerRegistry>` to every run so samples accumulate across runs; without one, no breaker applies.

Each breaker keeps the existing state machine: phase, probe ownership and failure count behind one mutex, with a generation counter so an outcome from a call admitted under an earlier generation is ignored. A step admitted while the breaker is closed retries per its policy and reports one outcome. A half-open probe gets exactly one attempt. An open breaker never invokes the step, and the step ends `NotRun(CircuitOpen)`. Cancellation and interruption are not reported as breaker failures.

A client error (HTTP 4xx other than 408 and 429) is reported to the breaker as a success: the downstream answered and rejected this one request, which says it is up. Counting a caller's 404s or 400s as failures would let one bad input open the breaker for every caller of that key. 408 and 429 (the downstream is slow or shedding load), 5xx, timeouts and other errors count as failures. This follows Envoy's outlier detection, which ejects a host on consecutive 5xx and resets on any other response.

Retries are jittered. Without `ExecOptions::jitter_seed`, each retry's jitter seed is derived from the run id, step id and attempt number (FNV-1a with a splitmix64 finalizer, mapped to `[0, 1)`), so steps that fail together back off by different amounts instead of retrying in lockstep, while the same run and plan always wait the same delays. `jitter_seed(x)` fixes one seed for every retry of every step, as before.

Retries are budgeted per run with `michi_core::resilience::RetryBudget`, a pure helper modelled on tower's `TpsBudget`: each successful step deposits a fraction of a retry (10% by default), each retry withdraws one, the budget starts with a small reserve (10) and is capped (100). When the budget is empty the step stops retrying and ends with its last outcome. First attempts are never budgeted. `ExecOptions::no_retry_budget()` turns it off.

Retry only at one layer: a step whose own HTTP client already retries should use `RetryConfig` with zero retries here.

`michi-pipeline` re-exports `RetryConfig`, `RetryConfigError`, `RetryBudget` and `IdempotencyKey` from `michi_core::resilience`, so callers configure retries without a direct `michi-core` dependency:

```rust
use std::time::Duration;

use michi_pipeline::{ExecOptions, RetryBudget, RetryConfig};

let options = ExecOptions::new()
    .retry(RetryConfig::new(3, Duration::from_millis(100), Duration::from_secs(5), 0.2))
    .retry_budget(RetryBudget::new(0.1, 10, 100));
```

## Observer

`ExecOptions::observer(Arc<dyn StepObserver>)` is called synchronously from the scheduler loop. `on_step_started` fires before a step is spawned and `on_step_finished` fires with each step's terminal `StepRecord`, including skipped steps and, on resume, steps carried over. A closure `Fn(&RunId, &StepRecord)` implements it. Persisting each finished record, plus `StepRecord::in_flight(id, name)` for each started one, lets a caller rebuild the run with `RunRecord::from_parts` after a crash. An append-only log is enough: `from_parts` keeps the last record saved for each step, so a step that started and finished rebuilds as finished. Resume then treats a step still `Running` as ambiguous instead of re-running it blindly.

The observer is caller code, so a panic in it is caught (`std::panic::catch_unwind`) rather than unwinding the scheduler, which would lose the record and drop every running step. The run carries on, the observer is still called for later events, and `RunRecord::observer_panics()` counts the caught panics. A non-zero count means the observer missed events, so progress it persisted may be incomplete. The process's panic hook still runs.

## Resume

`resume(&prior, &plan, &ResumeOptions).await` continues an interrupted run. It returns `Err(ResumeError)` before running anything if the plan's fingerprint differs from the record's (`FingerprintMismatch`), the record names a step the plan lacks (`UnknownStep`), or a step marked verified is not awaiting verification (`NotAwaitingVerification`).

- It always runs under the prior record's `RunId`, so idempotency keys stay stable. There is no way to resume under a new id.
- `Completed` and `CompletedEarlier` steps are never re-run; they become `CompletedEarlier`.
- `Failed`, `Skipped`, `NotRun` and `Pending` steps (and steps missing from the record) run again.
- `OutcomeUnknown`, `Panicked` and `Running` steps run again only if the step is `Replay::Idempotent`. Otherwise they keep their prior record, and their dependents are skipped, until the caller marks them with `ResumeOptions::verified(id, Verification::Applied)` (treated as `CompletedEarlier`) or `Verification::NotApplied` (run again).

Resume indexes the prior record's steps once (every record lists each step once: `from_parts` keeps the last saved record per step and deserializing rejects a repeated step), so preparing a resume is O(N log N) in the step count: 50,000 carried-over steps took 1.6 s with a linear lookup per step and take about 20 ms now. `RunRecord::step(id)` is still a linear scan; index `steps()` yourself to look up many. `Plan::new` likewise drops repeated dependencies with an O(1) check per edge, so a wide fan-in is linear.

Resume is forward recovery and at least once per step: michi has no atomic commit between a step's effect and the record, so a step can run again if the process stopped after its effect but before its record was saved. Effects are exactly once only when the step hands `idempotency_key()` to a downstream that deduplicates. Resume is not incremental recomputation: it does not notice that a completed step's inputs changed.

## Non-goals

Dynamic dependencies, data passing between steps, cross-run concurrency limits, compensation or sagas, durable storage, input-hash memoization and critical-path scheduling. A concise rendering mode (non-completed steps plus a completed count) is not built yet.

It returns `ResumeError::FingerprintMismatch` if the saved fingerprint is not the plan's and `ResumeError::UnknownStep` for a saved step the plan lacks. When `steps` holds several records for one step, the last one wins, so an append-only log of `StepRecord::in_flight` on start and the finished record on finish rebuilds each step's latest status. A plan step with no saved record is `Pending`.
docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:154:`ExecOptions::observer(Arc<dyn StepObserver>)` is called synchronously from the scheduler loop. `on_step_started` fires before a step is spawned and `on_step_finished` fires with each step's terminal `StepRecord`, including skipped steps and, on resume, steps carried over. A closure `Fn(&RunId, &StepRecord)` implements it. Persisting each finished record, plus `StepRecord::in_flight(id, name)` for each started one, lets a caller rebuild the run with `RunRecord::from_parts` after a crash. An append-only log is enough: `from_parts` keeps the last record saved for each step, so a step that started and finished rebuilds as finished. Resume then treats a step still `Running` as ambiguous instead of re-running it blindly.
docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:156:The observer is caller code, so a panic in it is caught (`std::panic::catch_unwind`) rather than unwinding the scheduler, which would lose the record and drop every running step. The run carries on, the observer is still called for later events, and `RunRecord::observer_panics()` counts the caught panics. A non-zero count means the observer missed events, so progress it persisted may be incomplete. The process's panic hook still runs.

docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:167:Resume indexes the prior record's steps once (every record lists each step once: `from_parts` keeps the last saved record per step and deserializing rejects a repeated step), so preparing a resume is O(N log N) in the step count: 50,000 carried-over steps took 1.6 s with a linear lookup per step and take about 20 ms now. `RunRecord::step(id)` is still a linear scan; index `steps()` yourself to look up many. `Plan::new` likewise drops repeated dependencies with an O(1) check per edge, so a wide fan-in is linear.
docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:169:Resume is forward recovery and at least once per step: michi has no atomic commit between a step's effect and the record, so a step can run again if the process stopped after its effect but before its record was saved. Effects are exactly once only when the step hands `idempotency_key()` to a downstream that deduplicates. Resume is not incremental recomputation: it does not notice that a completed step's inputs changed.

## Pipeline integration review

**No graph migration regression confirmed.** The new `Dag` preserves declaration indices used by the scheduler, and its canonical form preserves the plan fingerprint for valid plans. The pipeline suite passed **118 tests** with all features. An independent probe checked **1,000 generated DAGs** against a separate topological-order implementation and confirmed declaration-independent fingerprints.

### High-priority issue found elsewhere in the pipeline

**Resume can repeat a non-idempotent effect after a non-retryable failure.** A step that commits an effect and returns `ExecutionError::Failed { retryable: false }` ends as `Failed`. [resume](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/exec.rs:338) automatically reruns every `Failed` step, ignoring the error’s replay safety. A temporary consumer probe produced `first_status=Failed, retryable=false, commits_after_resume=2`. The [error contract](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/error.rs:35) says `retryable: true` is the step’s assurance that repeating it is safe. This is a **pre-existing semantic defect**, not introduced by `michi-graph`. The terminal model needs to preserve whether an effect may have happened; a generic `Failed` status cannot safely drive resume.

**Crash recovery cannot fail closed when persistence of the in-flight marker fails.** [The scheduler](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/scheduler.rs:164) catches a panic from `on_step_started` and still dispatches the step. If that callback was persisting the in-flight marker, a later crash leaves no saved step record. [Reconstruction](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/record.rs:273) marks it `Pending`, and resume reruns it. A second probe reproduced two effects after such a missing save. The [spec](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:154) acknowledges incomplete persistence after observer panics and promises at-least-once execution, so this is a **documented guarantee gap**, not a graph regression. It matters for consumers expecting crash-safe mutation replay: `StepObserver` has no failure result that can stop dispatch.

### Migration-specific concerns

- [Plan construction](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/plan.rs:299) now goes through graph key and edge sorting. The repeated-edge lookup no longer dominates, but total graph construction is not linear in general. This is a performance claim to correct and benchmark at realistic plan sizes; I did not measure a production-scale regression.
- [Violation translation](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/michi-hardening/crates/michi-pipeline/src/plan.rs:374) maps every future `michi_graph::Violation` variant to `TooManySteps`. Because the graph dependency is intended to use a compatible version range, a future variant could become a misleading error. This is a maintainability risk, not a current failing case.

A caller can resume a record against changed effects under the same step IDs and dependencies. The spec assigns that responsibility to callers; the API should avoid presenting the fingerprint as a complete semantic identity.
